data.narrative:
Pacific Fusion, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Eric Lander and Will Regan, has raised $900M to date. The broader nuclear energy sector comprises 11 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy—though direct stage and valuation alignment within this set remains limited.

Stage-progression analysis applies a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $900M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $1.8B. This method is the only quantitatively reliable approach available; peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient data density within narrow filters (only one same-stage comparable identified across the nuclear energy universe), and a broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of the peer set.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.5B to $2.1B, with a median of $1.8B. This reflects the stage-progression result with reasonable variance bounds. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.0x multiplier for this sector and stage, the absence of direct peer valuation anchors, and the lack of visibility into Pacific Fusion's specific capital deployment and technical progress relative to named competitors. A more robust analysis would benefit from narrower peer comparables at equivalent stages and valuations.
